# GTNH Speedrun LiveSplit

Splits LiveSplit on milestones that the [GTNH Speedrun Audit](../gtnh-speedrun-audit) mod logs. The server has a
catalog of named milestones. Each runner picks which milestones are the segments of the runner's LiveSplit file. The
timer starts when the audit starts timing. Each split happens when its milestone is first reached, with LiveSplit's
game time set to the in-game time (IGT) of that moment.

A runner who joins a run in progress gets the run so far: their timer starts and splits each milestone already
reached, at the IGT of the milestone's first reach.

## Joining a run in progress

When a runner joins, the runner's client gets the catalog, then every milestone reached so far, in the order reached,
then the current IGT. The client turns them into splits of the runner's route. A runner who rejoins gets the same
list, and no segment splits twice.

The server rebuilds the list from the audit log on each start, so a server restart loses nothing. LiveSplit's Game
Time of a caught-up split is the IGT of the milestone. The split's Real Time is the moment of the catch-up.

After a rollback (a backup restore, or a crash before the world was saved), the milestones that the world lost are
gone from the list. On rejoin, the timer is unsplit back to the milestones the world still has. The timer splits a
lost milestone again when the run reaches the milestone again, at the new IGT. The lost lines stay in the audit log.

The server is the authority. While the run is going, the client checks the timer about once a second, and a split made
by hand past the server's list is undone.

- A milestone id: the segment takes the milestone's name and icon.
- `{"id": …}` with a `name` or an `icon` for the segment. A name that starts with `-` is a subsplit in LiveSplit.
- `allOf`: for milestones a run can reach in any order. The segment splits when the last of them is reached, at that
  milestone's IGT.
- `anyOf`: the segment splits at the first of them.

LiveSplit splits its segments in a fixed order. When a later segment is reached first, `skipMissedSplits` decides what
happens (see [Config](#config)). Group milestones that come in any order with `allOf`.

The client reads the file on each join. A segment with a milestone id that the server doesn't have is left out, and chat
lists the ids. A file that can't be read is an empty route, and chat says why. Export the LiveSplit file again after you
change your route.

- `/livesplit milestones [page]`: the server's milestones, with ids and the IGT of each one reached.
- `/livesplit route [page]`: your segments, with the IGT of each one reached, or how many milestones of a group are
  reached.
- `/livesplit export`: write the LiveSplit file of your route.

## 2. Rule 12: a label on a constant or a field

`core/rules/comments.md`, after the two examples of `R12-no-name-phrase`. A draft for your approval:

```
  A label is fine on a constant, an enum constant or a field when the label says what the name
  doesn't, such as the look of a style. The label doesn't start with `The`, and doesn't have a
  method as the subject:
  - `` {@link #addVertices} adds a small square in the middle of the block `` on `SQUARE` →
    `A small square in the middle of an untinted block.`
  When a better name says the same, rename the field, as for `size` above.
```

Also a `decisions.jsonl` entry, `R12-label-constant`, that quotes your answer.
